column1: # The detectors this PUBLIC repository carries in the open. One row per detector, tab separated:
#   name <TAB> category <TAB> flags <TAB> pattern <TAB> canary template
# `flags` is `-` or `i` (case-insensitive). `pattern` is a Python regular expression, matched over
# BYTES with re.MULTILINE. `canary template` is the fresh negative-of-a-negative: text whose `{n:a}`
# placeholders are replaced with n bytes drawn from /dev/urandom over the named alphabet `a`
# (.github/held/held_content_scan.py, ALPHABETS). Every scan draws one canary per row and refuses to
# report anything unless each row matched ITS OWN canary. A detector that no longer fires is a
# detector that cannot find what it is for, and a clean result from it means nothing.
# These rows are a port of the credential half of the public leak check that guards every push and
# every `gh` write from Theorem's machines (theorem-labs/agent-infra, tag leak-check-v13,
# `public_leak_check.py` LEAK_SECRET and LEAK_SECRET_VALUE, and its `draw_canaries`). They are here
# in the clear because a credential's published FORMAT is public knowledge -- every scanner ships
# the same list -- and because a detector a contributor can read is one they can satisfy before
# The other half of that check reads for content this repository holds back. Those patterns name
# what they look for, so they are not in a public file: they are loaded from the Actions secret
# HELD_CONTENT_RULES, in exactly this format, and pinned by row count and sha256 in
# .github/held/private-detectors.sha256. A missing, short or altered private table fails the job;
# it never silently shrinks the scan.
# A format match is refused even in a test fixture: this check cannot tell a throwaway key from a
# live one. Write a fixture credential so it does not match (see must-pass-lines.txt), or do not
